newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech still sees early 97 long distance.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech still sees early 97 long distance.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Tuesday it is still aiming for early 1997 to begin offering long distance services, a market it sees as a potentially very profitable.

"We're looking forward to being in the long-distance business sometime early in 1997," Oren Schaffer, chief financial officer of Ameritech, said in an interview. "That's a very nice revenue opportunity for us, so we're anxious that the markets open up."

A U.S. court on Tuesday extended a stay on key provisions of the landmark Telecommunications Act which brings competition to local markets and allows regional bell operating companies such as Ameritech to offer long-distance service.
At this point, Ameritech said it does not see the ruling stopping it from entering that market.

"We don't know that it does anything in stopping our ability to enter long distance," Dave Pacholczyk, a spokesman specializing in regulatory issues, said after the ruling. "The Telecommmunications Act itself still exists," he said.

Schaffer said Ameritech has filed checklists showing local competition required by the Act for it to enter long distance. He said the checklists have been filed for state certification in Michigan, Illinois and Ohio and will be filed in Wisconsin and Indiana by month's end.
"We clearly are ready," Schaffer said, adding Ameritech's long-distance market is about $9 billion to $9.5 billion, after paying access fees.
Earlier Tuesday, Ameritech reported third quarter earnings of $0.94 a share, up from $0.92 last year. Excluding one-time gains, Ameritech reported earnings of $0.84 last year.
The earnings were in line with analysts expectations.

"Another very strong quarter," said Bob Venable, an analyst with Robert W. Baird & Co. "They've had very consistent and impressive growth in their core businesses and seem to be very focussed on delivering what they promised to their shareholders."

Nonetheless, Venable said he rates Ameritech stock a hold. He said he is concerned about how it and other Baby Bells will handle increased local competition, while he sees its entrance into long distance possibly dragging out into mid 1997 or beyond.
"It's very difficult to predict when this will play out and who is going to win, but in the meantime this is another very solid quarter," Venable said.

Ameritech said its access lines increased 3.7 percent in third quarter versus the previous year to 19.6 million lines. Cellular customers increased 37 percent to 2.3 million customers and paging customers rose 45 percent to 1.05 million, the company said.
